name: Yousef Abdulaziz
availability: Open to frontend and full-stack work
headline: I build interfaces that feel fast, and tooling that gets out of the way.
intro: Frontend engineer in Cairo with two years of shipping product UI. I work mostly in TypeScript — React and TanStack on the front, Node and Python when the interface needs something behind it.
focus: Type-safe data flow end to end

about.lede: Two years of product UI, and a habit of taking the slow step out of a workflow. Most of what I build sits where a type boundary and a screen meet.
paragraphs: Most of my work starts at the interface and works backwards. That usually means a strict type boundary at the edge — validated once, then trusted — and components that own their state instead of borrowing it from three layers up.

Outside product work I build tools I want to use: a terminal HTTP client, a set of Zod refiners, a search layer over a classical Arabic corpus. The pattern is the same — remove the step that makes you leave the thing you are doing.

playbook.title: Types at the edge
playbook.body: Validate once, where data enters: a request, a JSON file, a content edit. Past that boundary the types are honest, so nothing downstream has to defend itself.

playbook.title: State next to the change
playbook.body: A component owns the state it renders. Pushing it three layers up is usually a sign the boundary was drawn in the wrong place.

playbook.title: Delete the detour
playbook.body: curlz exists so an API request does not need a browser tab. siyar-search exists so a citation does not need a page-flip. A tool that removes no step is a toy.

playbook.title: Small scoped changes
playbook.body: One ticket, one reviewable diff, one green build. It is how a crew of agents ships real software here, and it is why the codebase still reads cleanly a year later.
